items.title: Police Call Mississauga Stabbing an Isolated Incident as Search for Second Suspect Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police say the Mississauga stabbing that left one person fighting for their life is believed to be an isolated incident with no ongoing threat to public safety. The outlet reports one suspect was taken into custody at the scene while officers continued searching the surrounding area for a second suspect. INsauga reports police describe the outstanding suspect as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four, with blonde and brown hair. According to the outlet, the victim remained in critical condition at a trauma centre as of the latest police update. INsauga reports officers remained in the Main Street and Dundas Street East area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Proposed for Dixie Site Head to Planning Committee
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council approve a rezoning application that would bring two 16-storey apartment towers to a 3-acre site at 1225 Dundas Street East in the Dixie neighbourhood. The outlet reports the towers would be connected by a six-storey podium and contain a combined 553 residential rental units, along with ground-floor commercial space. Mississauga.com reports the proposal also includes 34 four-storey back-to-back townhouses, bringing the total to 587 residential units. According to the outlet, the site is owned by a group of five investment companies, including Stephen-Mitchell Realty Limited and Whitehorn Investments Limited. Mississauga.com reports a city staff report noted the property sits within a designated intensification area meant to accommodate significant growth, with Mississauga's planning committee set to vote on the application September 8.

items.title: Police Release Suspect Photos After 32 Vehicle Break-Ins Hit Three Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Peel Regional Police have released photos of a suspect wanted in connection with at least 32 vehicle break-ins in Mississauga. The outlet reports the break-ins occurred on September 3 in the Alpha Mills Road, Falconer Drive and Plainsman Road areas. CityNews Toronto reports all of the vehicles were unoccupied at the time and that nothing was taken during the incidents. According to the outlet, the suspect is described as a white man approximately 30 years old with a medium build. CityNews Toronto reports he was last seen wearing a jacket with the word POLO written on the back collar, joggers, and two-toned shoes with a white sole, while carrying a backpack.

items.title: Square One, Celebration Square Among Mississauga Spots Staying Open Over Labour Day
items.summary: According to INsauga, several Mississauga businesses and attractions will remain open on Labour Day, September 7, even as most government offices and services close for the holiday. The outlet reports Square One Shopping Centre will be open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room, The Food District, Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket. INsauga reports Celebration Square and its fountain, select Rabba grocery stores and Beer Store locations, the city's YMCA health and fitness centre, and the Mississauga Chinese Centre will also be open, alongside movie theatres and many restaurants, cafes and bars. According to the outlet, Mississauga City Hall and Region of Peel offices will be closed for the day, along with banks, libraries and some community centres, and there will be no Canada Post pickup or delivery. INsauga reports garbage and recycling collection will be pushed back one day, MiWay will run on a regular Sunday schedule, and GO Transit will operate on a Saturday schedule.

items.title: MiWay Drops Route 110A as University Express Service Ramps Up for the School Year
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, MiWay is adjusting its bus schedule starting Tuesday, September 7, increasing service on some of its busiest corridors as students return to school. The outlet reports the changes include more frequent service on Route 110 University Express, which connects downtown Mississauga, the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, the Erin Mills community and Clarkson GO Station. Mississauga.com reports MiWay will discontinue its Route 110A University Express as part of the increased service on the main route. According to the outlet, two other routes will see reduced service due to lower ridership. Mississauga.com reports the schedule changes are also timed to resume regular school-day bus runs alongside the start of the new academic year.

items.title: GO Trains Diverted Around Port Credit After Saturday Night Lakeshore West Incident
items.summary: According to CP24, a person was struck by a GO train in Mississauga on Saturday night, prompting a shutdown of part of the Lakeshore West line. The outlet reports the circumstances surrounding the incident were not immediately known. CP24 reports the incident caused significant delays, with no train service between Port Credit and Exhibition stations. According to the outlet, GO Transit ran express buses between Port Credit and Kipling GO stations to help riders get around the closure. CP24 reports two train trips on the Lakeshore East line were also cancelled as a result of the incident.

items.title: Mississauga Accounts for Most of Peel's 300 Reported Vehicle Thefts Over Past Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton between August 5 and September 5, with more than half taken from Mississauga owners. The outlet reports 178 of those thefts occurred in Mississauga, 118 in Brampton, and the remaining four were not assigned a location on the force's crime map. INsauga reports the map identified hot spots including Toronto Pearson International Airport and the Square One shopping centre in Mississauga, along with the area of Bovaird Drive and Highway 410 in Brampton. According to the outlet, Brampton saw more violent crime over the same period, with 190 of a combined 320 reported assaults, or more than 59 per cent, occurring there compared with 127 in Mississauga. INsauga reports the data also showed 24 combined robberies across both cities, with six reported in Mississauga and 18 in Brampton.
